# ElectronIx Trace

> Per-unit product traceability software for manufacturing plants. Built by
> ElectronIx in Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu, India. On-premise, offline-first,
> Rust and PostgreSQL. Quoted per plant, not per seat.

## What it does

ElectronIx Trace records what went into every unit a plant builds, what was done
to it, who did it, on which machine, and what it measured. Scanning the code on
the finished product returns that unit's complete, auditable history.

The two queries it exists to answer:

- Backward trace (unit to history): scan a returned unit and get its job card,
  BOM revision, every component serial and lot consumed, every torque value,
  every test reading, every operator, and any rework.
- Forward trace (component or machine to units): given a bad supplier lot, or a
  machine that drifted out of calibration between two times, list every finished
  unit affected. This is the recall query and it is an indexed lookup.

## Who it is for

Indian MSME and mid-size discrete manufacturers: auto components and Tier 1/2
suppliers, pumps and valves, switchgear and electrical panels, EV components,
precision machining and export engineering, general line and batch assembly.
Typically 50 to 500 people, under OEM or customer traceability requirements,
priced out of enterprise MES suites.

## Key characteristics

- Offline-first: stations write every event to durable local storage before any
  network call and replay idempotently. Internet is not required at any point.
- A lapsed subscription never stops production capture. There is no enforcement
  state in the software that halts capture; it restricts configuration changes
  and cloud sync only.
- Records are append-only with a per-unit SHA-256 hash chain. Corrections are new
  rows that supersede old ones with a reason and an operator, never edits.
- Raw device payloads are stored verbatim beside each parsed value.
- Every limit is configuration: capture points hold min, max, nominal, sampling
  rule and whether they are mandatory. Changing a torque window is not a release.
- Routes are validated graphs with parallel branches, optional operations and
  rework loops, guarded by eight gate types.
- Labels: your own template, versioned with an effective date, rendered as native
  ZPL II to TCP port 9100 with no OS print driver. Direct part marking with Data
  Matrix and mark read-back for parts that go through wash, paint or heat.
- Deployment: one edge box per plant running PostgreSQL 16 on hardware you own.
  Signed over-the-air updates verify before download, apply atomically and roll
  back automatically; the offline USB path uses identical verification.

## What it is not

- Not certified. No ISO 9001, IATF 16949, FDA or 21 CFR Part 11 certification for
  the software or the company. It produces evidence for an audit; it does not
  confer compliance.
- Not an MES. No scheduling, OEE, downtime analysis, maintenance planning or work
  instruction authoring.
- No ERP connector. There is a documented seam for a work-order source and a
  field to hold an external reference, but no built SAP, Oracle or Tally
  integration.
- Not a hosted cloud service today. The schema is multi-tenant; the hosted
  multi-plant service is a later phase.
- PostgreSQL only. MySQL is explicitly not supported.
